title: The Tamil People Are No Longer Ready to Be Deceived!
translatorNote: This translation is intended to carry Kalaignar's voice into clear, contemporary English rather than recast the letter as literary or academic prose. It preserves the source's argument, political directness, rhetorical questions, repetition, irony, factual detail, and paragraph order. Names, dates, figures, quotations, and intentional English expressions are retained. Where Tamil idiom cannot be reproduced literally without sounding unnatural, the English follows its sense and rhetorical force without adding claims absent from the source. The original Tamil is reproduced in full below the translation and remains the authoritative text. `Udanpirappē` is retained in Tamil transliteration rather than flattened into “brother,” “sister,” or “comrade.” Literally evoking “one born alongside me,” Kalaignar uses it as a distinctive address of shared identity, equality, affection, and solidarity within the movement.
paragraphs: I read in the newspapers what Chief Minister Jayalalithaa had ordered in the Tamil Nadu Government’s press release dated 7 October 2013. I was delighted. Do you know why? Announcements worth several crores of rupees had been poured out about the Tamil language, the Chief Minister’s interest in it, the Tirukkural, the Tolkāppiyam and Sangam Tamil.
You ask how many crores these schemes amount to? Do not be impatient; I shall explain them myself.

The Honourable Chief Minister of Tamil Nadu, Selvi J. Jayalalithaa, has ordered that a Tirukkural art gallery with excellent infrastructure be established at the International Institute of Tamil Studies in Taramani, Chennai, at an estimated cost of ten lakh rupees.
You may decide for yourselves how large an art gallery can be created for this estimate of ten lakh rupees!
Do you know what is to be housed in that gallery?

Paintings illustrating the Tirukkural are to be displayed; editions of the Tirukkural rendered as paintings are to be collected and exhibited; prose editions are to be collected and displayed; visual presentations, short films and animated films connected with the Tirukkural are to be collected and screened; students of Government colleges of fine arts and other artists are to produce contemporary paintings of the ethical ideas expressed in the Tirukkural; translations of the Tirukkural in different languages are to be collected and exhibited; and versions in Vatteluttu and stone inscriptions are to be gathered and displayed.
How immense is the concern this Government has for the Tirukkural and Thiruvalluvar!

Only a few months ago, Daily Thanthi itself carried a report with photographs under the headline: “Without Proper Maintenance, Valluvar Kottam Is Becoming a Shelter for Anti-social Elements—The Misery of Its Becoming a Refuge for Hired Lovers.” The report stated:

Chennai’s Valluvar Kottam, lacking proper maintenance, is turning into a haunt of anti-social elements and a refuge for hired lovers. Couples have written love poems and love symbols upon the stone inscriptions carrying the Tirukkural. Drinkers are using Valluvar Kottam as an open-air bar.

Valluvar Kottam is a vast auditorium situated in the heart of Chennai. This Government has not even maintained it properly. Fine Tirukkural visual displays have already been installed there. Leaving those neglected, they now say they are going to create another Tirukkural art gallery at Taramani. It brings to mind the proverb: “The man who cannot climb the roof to catch a chicken claims that he will tear open the sky and show Vaikuntham.”
The Thiruvalluvar statue erected at Kanyakumari under the DMK Government was also left without maintenance by the AIADMK Government. In a statement I issued, I said:

If the AIADMK Government does not allocate the necessary funds and promptly carry out the maintenance of Ayya Valluvar’s statue, we are considering whether the Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam itself should organise a major agitation to draw the rulers’ attention.
Only after that were maintenance works properly carried out by the Government.

Next, it is said that the Honourable Chief Minister has ordered the establishment, at the International Institute of Tamil Studies, of a World Tamil Cultural Reception and Information Centre equipped with excellent infrastructure and modern facilities. Do you know how many crores have been allocated for it? Here too, the estimate is only ten lakh rupees.

When such grand schemes are announced to honour the Tirukkural and Thiruvalluvar, can Tolkāppiyar be left out? What is the Chief Minister’s order? She has ordered the creation of a Tolkāppiyar Research Chair at the International Institute of Tamil Studies, allocating fifty lakh rupees for it.

Yet the park opened under the DMK Government as “Tolkāppiya Poonga” had that distinguished name changed under the AIADMK Government to “Adyar Poonga.” These are the people who now say they will establish a Tolkāppiyar Research Chair.

This announcement was contained in the Government press release of 7 October 2013 and appeared in all newspapers. But five months earlier, on 14 May 2013, the very same Chief Minister, Jayalalithaa, had read a statement under Rule 110 in the Tamil Nadu Legislative Assembly. In that statement she said:

I am pleased to announce that a research chair bearing the name of the Tolkāppiyam, which portrays the richness of Tamil life, will be established at the International Institute of Tamil Studies. A deposit of fifty lakh rupees will be provided to the Institute for this purpose.

Having made that announcement once, she has now made it again as though it were new and issued it as a Government press release. The people of Tamil Nadu must decide what name should be given to this practice.
Along with that announcement on 14 May 2013, the Chief Minister made another declaration:

Just as the Statue of Liberty presents the greatness and fame of the United States to the world, a Tamil Thai statue displaying to the world the civilisation, culture, literary wealth and architectural skill of the Tamil people will be erected at Madurai at an estimated cost of one hundred crore rupees.

The Opposition members in the Assembly praised and celebrated the Chief Minister for making this declaration. Five months have passed. Has the Tamil Thai statue been erected? Has even its inauguration already taken place by video conference?

Jayalalithaa also announced that a “Tamil Thai Poonga” would be created there, with models of the five landscapes—kurinji, mullai, marutham, neithal and paalai—and with the trees, plants and creepers mentioned in Sangam literature as evidence of Tamil antiquity. Where has that park been created?

All we can see is the cruelty of the present Government allowing both the Semmozhi Poonga and the Tolkāppiyar Poonga—built with great effort under the DMK administration—to wither without proper maintenance. The Tamil Thai Poonga itself is nowhere to be seen.
Even this announcement appears to be a renamed version of one I made in the concluding address of the World Classical Tamil Conference held at Coimbatore under the DMK Government:

Two thousand years ago, during the Sangam age, our ancestors classified Tamil land ecologically into the five landscapes of kurinji, mullai, marutham, neithal and paalai. Traditional genetic heritage parks based on these five landscapes will be established by the Tamil Nadu Government.
I wonder whether that announcement has now changed its name and become “Tamil Thai Poonga.”
Indeed, as early as the 2010–2011 Budget, paragraph 115 announced under the DMK Government:

On the 14.15 acres of land at Tallakulam in Madurai, which was allotted and levelled in 1982 for the World Tamil Sangam, the “Tolkāppiyar World Tamil Sangam” will be established. A gallery displaying the high achievements of Tamil Nadu in art, literature and culture will be created; an auditorium will be constructed to support Tamils and Tamil research worldwide; and statues of Sangam poets and Tamil scholars will be designed and installed in proper chronological order.
At the end of her announcement, Chief Minister Jayalalithaa stated that these measures would promote the development of the Tamil language and make Tamil culture known throughout the world.
At this point, shall I remind you of just a few achievements for Tamil under the DMK Government?

- In 1970, the song beginning “Nīrārum Kadaludutha,” written by Manonmaniam Sundaranar, was made the Tamil Thai Vazhthu. - A separate ministry was created for Tamil as the official language and for Tamil culture. - The Directorate of the Senthamizh Etymological Dictionary Project was established. - The International Institute of Tamil Studies was created. - A committee of Tamil scholars was appointed to write the history of Tamil Nadu. - A grant of seventy-five lakh rupees was given to Dravidian University. - Histories of Tamil Nadu were published as books. - Fifty lakh rupees was provided to establish a Tamil Chair at the University of Malaya. - The century-old dream of securing classical-language status for Tamil was realised. - The World Classical Tamil Conference was held. - A 133-foot statue of Thiruvalluvar was erected at Kanyakumari, and Valluvar Kottam was created in Chennai. - Tax exemption was granted to films given Tamil titles. - Tamil was made compulsory for all students up to Standard Ten, and priority in employment was provided to those educated through Tamil. - “Madras State” was renamed “Tamil Nadu.” - “Madras” was renamed “Chennai.” - At the Coimbatore Classical Tamil Conference, it was announced that a special fund of one hundred crore rupees would be created by the Tamil Nadu Government exclusively for the development of Tamil, and a Government Order was issued for it.
The list could go on. But what qualifications do those who now issue statements claiming to labour for Tamil’s development possess?

Under the DMK Government, the Pavendhar Classical Tamil Research Library was opened in the present Secretariat. Researchers and enthusiasts used the rare ancient Tamil books and manuscripts housed there. Where is that library now? Immediately after the 2011 election and the AIADMK’s assumption of office, they removed the library from that building, took its books somewhere else, and made them inaccessible. Are these the people who are going to develop Tamil?

Every year in the Legislative Assembly, after the Governor delivered his address in English, it was customary for the Speaker to read its Tamil translation. The AIADMK Government abolished that practice. When DMK members questioned the decision, the Government replied, “There is no time.” Are those the people who will develop Tamil?
On 10 May 2013, they announced in the Assembly that English-medium sections would be opened in middle schools, high schools and higher secondary schools. Are those the people who will develop Tamil?
In the Samacheer Kalvi textbooks printed under the DMK Government, they pasted “stickers” over even the picture of Thiruvalluvar. Are those noble souls the people who will develop Tamil?

The Avvaiyar Award, which was to be presented by the Tamil Development Department, was removed from that department and transferred elsewhere—and then given to a person with no Tamil scholarship. Are those rulers the people who will develop Tamil?
Leaving the Anna Centenary Library without proper maintenance, and removing the Kannagi statue—a cultural symbol of Tamil Nadu—are these the acts of people devoted to the Tamil nation?

Consider the Central Institute of Classical Tamil. Under the DMK Government, efforts were made both to secure classical-language status for Tamil and to establish its central institute in Tamil Nadu. What is its condition today?

From my personal funds I gave one crore rupees to the Institute, asking that the interest be used to present, once every year, an award worth ten lakh rupees. When the Classical Tamil Conference was held at Coimbatore under the DMK Government, the award was presented to Thiru Asko Parpola. Two years have passed since then, yet the award has not been presented again. Neither the AIADMK Government nor Chief Minister Jayalalithaa has taken any step to continue it. Such is the lady’s love for classical Tamil and for the Tamil people!

These are the people who now issue announcements about a Tirukkural art exhibition, a Tolkāppiyar Research Chair and a Sangam Tamil gallery, imagining that they can deceive us. The Tamil people are no longer ready to be deceived!
With affection, M. K. 10 October 2013
